speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe exactly what this skin condition on your left dorsal hand looks like? Is it raised, scaly, or perhaps blistering?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that background. To better understand the nature of the lesion, do you notice if the skin on your hand appears thickened, waxy, or has a "pebbly" texture, and does it seem particularly shiny compared to the rest of your arm?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the description of a rough, scaly plaque on the dorsum of your hand in an older adult with significant sun exposure, I suspect this is actinic keratosis or potentially squamous cell carcinoma. REQUEST TEST: Skin biopsy of the left dorsal hand lesion. REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy of the left dorsal hand lesion.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin Biopsy: Hyperkeratosis with parakeratosis, solar elastosis, and atypical keratinocytes confined to the epidermis. Consistent with actinic keratosis. Vital Signs: Temperature 36.8°C (98.2°F), Blood Pressure 130/85 mmHg, Heart Rate 72 bpm, Respiratory Rate 14 breaths/min. Dermatological Exam: Rough, scaly plaque on left dorsal hand; no tenderness or pain on palpation.
